The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

## Implementation Plan: Supplement Brand Landing Variants

### Phase Order (Agent Dispatch Sequence)

**Phase 0 — KB Gap Fill (parallel, blocks Phase 2)**
- `decoder` runs supplements teardown queue (Ritual, AG1, Hims, Care/of, Magic Spoon, Liquid IV) and writes to `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/ecom-brand-teardowns.md`. Output: 5 above-fold patterns + below-fold rhythms + objection ladders. **Blocks variant differentiation.**
- `decoder` also drafts `trust-social-proof-patterns.md` (gap) — needed for variant 3/4 trust stacks.

**Phase 1 — Scaffold (sequential, no blockers)**
- `riko` scaffolds Vite + React 19 + TS strict + Tailwind 4 + shadcn at the empty cwd. Installs `react-router-dom@7`, `lucide-react`, `class-variance-authority`, `tailwind-merge`. Configures `tsconfig.json` with `"strict": true, "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true`. Adds shadcn primitives: button, accordion, sheet (cart drawer), tabs, badge, separator, dialog (exit-intent).

**Phase 2 — Brand + Tokens (parallel after Phase 0)**
- `decoder` picks niche (recommend: cognitive/nootropic OR women's hormonal — underserved vs AG1's general-wellness saturation) and invents brand name + product.
- `token` derives palette from chosen niche → emits `src/lib/tokens.ts` + Tailwind 4 `@theme` block in `src/index.css` (CSS-first config, no `tailwind.config.js`). Tokens: `--color-brand-*`, `--radius-*`, `--ease-*`, `--shadow-*`.
- `quill` ratifies voice (1-page brand bible).

**Phase 3 — Copy (parallel, depends on Phase 2)**
- `spark` writes 5 distinct above-fold hooks (one per variant) targeting 40%+ lift archetypes.
- `merch` writes shared below-fold: benefits, ingredient stories, FAQ (using objection-handling-library.md top-5), review quotes.
- `ecom-cro` specs interactive mechanics inventory.

**Phase 4 — Build (sequential, the long phase)**
- `elio` + `koda` build shared components first, then 5 variants.
- `catalyst` orchestrates variant differentiation reviews.

**Phase 5 — QA**
- `sage` reviews TS strictness, a11y (axe pass), responsive breakpoints, token discipline (no hardcoded hex).
- `luna` writes light smoke tests: each route renders, sticky-bar appears <768px, accordion toggles, subscribe toggle updates price.
- `vega` final design approval.
- `mira` captures lessons.

### Project Structure
```
src/
  variants/
    Variant1Spec.tsx        // spec-hero (data-dense, "the science")
    Variant2Lifestyle.tsx   // lifestyle-static (aspirational photo, soft CTA)
    Variant3Split.tsx       // split-hero (ingredient transparency left, hero right)
    Variant4Video.tsx       // video-override style (autoplay loop placeholder, founder-voice)
    Variant5Clinical.tsx    // scientific-credibility (citations, doctor endorsements)
  components/shared/
    ProductCard.tsx, BundleSelector.tsx, SubscribeToggle.tsx,
    StickyAddToCart.tsx, CartDrawer.tsx, IngredientModule.tsx,
    ReviewDistribution.tsx, FAQAccordion.tsx, TrustBar.tsx,
    ExitIntent.tsx, Nav.tsx, Footer.tsx
  pages/
    Index.tsx               // `/` — 5 variant thumbnails, iframe previews + jump links
  data/
    mock.ts                 // Product, Reviews, Ingredients, Bundles, Testimonials
  lib/
    tokens.ts, cn.ts, types.ts
  App.tsx                   // Router
```

### Variant Differentiation (psychology, not color)
1. **Spec-hero** — "5 actives, 0 fillers" data table above fold, rational buyer.
2. **Lifestyle** — full-bleed model shot, single sentence promise, emotional buyer.
3. **Split-hero** — left: ingredient close-up + dosage; right: product. Transparency-driven skeptic.
4. **Video/founder** — looping b-roll, founder quote overlay, narrative buyer.
5. **Clinical** — citation badges, NSF/3rd-party-tested, MD endorsement quote, authority buyer.

### Routing
**React Router 7** (`createBrowserRouter`). Simpler than page-switcher, gives real URLs for stakeholder shareback. Routes: `/`, `/variant-1` … `/variant-5`. Index uses scaled iframes for true side-by-side.

### Token Strategy
Tailwind 4 CSS-first via `@theme` in `index.css`. `token` agent outputs design tokens as CSS custom properties; `tokens.ts` re-exports as TS constants for inline-style edge cases. No `tailwind.config.js`.

### Mock Data Shape
`Product { id, name, slug, priceOnetime, priceSubscribe, servings, actives: Ingredient[] }`, `Ingredient { name, dosageMg, claim, citation? }`, `Review { rating, title, body, author, verified, date }`, `Bundle { id, products, discountPct }`, `Testimonial { quote, author, role, avatar }`. Seed: 847 reviews, 4.7 avg, distribution skewed realistically.

### CRO Mechanics
StickyAddToCart (mobile <768px), CartDrawer (Sheet), SubscribeToggle (saves 15%), BundleSelector (1/2/3-pack), FAQAccordion, IngredientModule (expand for citation), ReviewDistribution (5-star bar chart), ExitIntent (Dialog on mouseleave, desktop only).

### Quality Gates
`sage`: strict TS pass, a11y (focus traps in Sheet/Dialog, ARIA on accordion), no `any`, no inline hex. `luna`: 5 route render tests, sticky-bar viewport test, subscribe-toggle price math, accordion toggle. Skip E2E.

### Risk Callouts
- **Decoder backlog blocks Phase 2** — run Phase 0 first, do not parallelize with Phase 1 build temptation.
- **Tailwind 4 + shadcn compatibility** — shadcn CLI now supports v4; verify `riko` uses the v4-compatible registry, not v3 templates.
- **Variant sameness drift** — `catalyst` must enforce "different conversion psychology" rubric at Phase 4 mid-review or variants collapse into color swaps.
- **Trust KB gap** — if `decoder` skips `trust-social-proof-patterns.md`, variant 5 (clinical) ships weak.
- **Scope creep** — no real cart persistence, no checkout flow past drawer, no auth. State lives in `useState` + `useReducer`, no Zustand.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Test/Ecom Design testing/src/App.tsx
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Test/Ecom Design testing/src/index.css
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Test/Ecom Design testing/src/data/mock.ts
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Test/Ecom Design testing/src/lib/tokens.ts
- /Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Test/Ecom Design testing/src/components/shared/StickyAddToCart.tsx

Lock and return:

2. **Tagline** — 4-6 words, claim + closure pattern.
3. **Hero claim** — primary above-fold promise (one sentence).
4. **Product** — single SKU. Format (capsules / powder / drops / chewables), serving size, key actives (3-5 ingredients with dosage).

7. **Brand voice direction** — 3 adjectives + 1 anti-pattern. Hand off to `quill`.
8. **Top 3 buyer objections** — pulled from `~/.claude/memory/content/ecom/objection-handling-library.md` filtered to chosen niche.

## Constraints

- Brand must support spec-hero archetype = needs concrete numbers (mg dosing, study citations).
- Brand must support clinical archetype = needs MD-endorsable category.
- Avoid niches with FDA-prescription overlap (skip ED/hair-loss — that's Hims territory).

Brand bible. ~400 words. Save to `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Test/Ecom Design testing/src/data/brand.md` for the team to consume. Also return the bible content in your reply so I can hand to token + quill in parallel.

---

## Brand Bible — Vela Cognition

### Niche: Cognitive / Nootropic

Niche scored against all four candidates:

| Niche | CAGR | Premium price tolerance | Objection richness | All 5 archetypes fit |
|-------|------|------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| **Cognitive / nootropic** | **12-14%** | **$65-79+/mo** | **Highest** | **YES** |
| Women's hormonal | 5.6% | Medium | Medium | No — spec-hero weak |
| Longevity / NAD+ | 18% | Very high but ICP narrow | Medium | No — lifestyle/founder-video thin |
| Sleep / circadian | 5.1% | Low | Low | No — clinical archetype weak |

Cognitive wins because: (1) objection density is highest — "does it work / which ingredients / how long / safe to stack" — meaning spec-hero and clinical archetypes carry maximum weight; (2) premium clinical DTC tier is thin (fewer than 10 real players; Thesis, Mind Lab Pro, HVMN); (3) ICP breadth (knowledge workers, athletes, executives) makes all five archetypes land credibly.

---

### 1. Brand Name

**Selected: Vela**

Latin origin — sail / candle. Both meanings carry directed energy and illumination. One syllable on cadence, phonetically clean, avoids the "neuro/brain/smart" cliche that marks 90% of the category. .com feasible. The candle duality supports "precision-directed mental energy" for spec-hero/clinical variants and "light the way" for lifestyle/founder-video variants.

Candidates considered: Kairos (3 syllables, .com taken), Noor (geographic association risk in US market).

---

### 2. Tagline

**"Clarity. Every hour."**

Outcome + frequency. Mid-tagline period signals confidence, not question. "Every hour" implies all-day sustained effect — the primary differentiator vs single-dose competitors.

---

### 3. Hero Claim

"Vela is a precision-dosed nootropic engineered for sustained focus, working memory, and mental endurance — in the hours that count."

"Precision-dosed" is the spec-hero load-bearing phrase — signals intentional, transparent dosing vs proprietary-blend hiding.

---

### 4. Product

**Vela Focus Formula — 60 Capsules (30-day supply, 2 caps/day)**

Format: Capsules. MD-endorsable. Enables precise per-ingredient dosing disclosure.

| Ingredient | Dose | Role |
|------------|------|------|
| Citicoline (Cognizin branded) | 500 mg | Attention, working memory — 15+ human clinical studies |
| L-Theanine | 200 mg | Focus without jitter, alpha brainwave support |
| Bacopa Monnieri (45% bacosides) | 300 mg | Long-term memory encoding — 12-week RCTs |
| Lion's Mane Mushroom (30% beta-glucan) | 500 mg | NGF support, neuroprotection |
| Rhodiola Rosea (3% rosavins, 1% salidroside) | 200 mg | Mental fatigue resistance, cortisol modulation |

No proprietary blends. All doses at or above clinically studied thresholds. MD-endorsable without reservation.

---

### 5. Pricing

- One-time: **$79 / 30-day supply** ($2.63/day)
- Subscribe & save 15%: **$67/month** ($2.23/day)

Per-serving copy: "Less than your morning coffee. More than it delivers."

Positioned between Mind Lab Pro ($65-69) and Thesis ($79-119). Meaningfully above GNC/Amazon tier ($25-40).

---

### 6. Palette Direction (for token agent)

Reference brands: Ritual (cream + sage warmth), Hims supplement pages (midnight authority), Thesis (warm sand + forest green).

In words:
- Base: warm cream (#F7F4EF range) — not pure white, never sterile
- Primary: deep forest / midnight sage (#1C3A2F range) — authority, not cold pharma blue
- Accent: amber-warm gold (#C8963E range) — the "candle/vela" reference, CTAs and highlights only
- Text: near-black warm (#1A1A18)
- Avoid: electric blue, neon green, energy drink palette, pharmaceutical teal

Flex rule: spec-hero + clinical variants push dark forest base. Lifestyle + founder-video push cream base. Split-hero is the middle register.

---

### 7. Brand Voice (for quill)

Three adjectives: **Precise. Assured. Literate.**

Anti-pattern — never use: "Unlock your potential" and all its variants (unleash, maximize, supercharge, boost). If the sentence could appear on a GNC end-cap, rewrite it.

---

### 8. Top 3 Buyer Objections

**1. Efficacy: "Do nootropics actually work or is this pseudoscience?"**
Root: Category polluted by underdosed proprietary blends. Buyers burned by "clinically studied" language used with sub-threshold doses.
Response architecture: Named ingredients + specific doses + PubMed links + Cognizin branded ingredient (pre-validated by its own clinical program). Spec-hero and clinical variants address this above fold structurally.

**2. Safety: "Is it safe daily? Will it interact with medications?"**
Root: Cognitive supplements are associated with prescription stimulants in buyer perception.
Response architecture: All 5 ingredients non-stimulant, non-habit-forming, GRAS status. MD-endorsement card. NSF Certified for Sport / Informed Sport cert above fold.

**3. Timeframe: "How long before I feel something?"**
Root: Bacopa and Lion's Mane require 8-12 weeks; buyers who expect instant results churn early.
Response architecture: Two-track claims. "Day 1: sharper focus within 45-60 minutes (Citicoline + L-Theanine)." "Week 8: measurable working memory improvement (Bacopa 300mg, 12-week RCT)." Converts the long-term mechanism from objection into subscription reason.

---

### Archetype Fit

| Archetype | Fit | Load-bearing element |
|-----------|-----|---------------------|
| Spec-hero | Strong | Named dosing table, Cognizin, PubMed chips |
| Lifestyle | Strong | Performance identity, amber/sage palette |
| Split-hero | Strong | Capsule (tactile) + precision copy |
| Founder-video | Strong | "I refused to take proprietary blends" narrative |
| Clinical | Strong | MD card, per-ingredient study chip, "4 RCTs" stat |

## Brand Bible — Vela Cognition

### Niche: Cognitive / Nootropic

Niche scored against all four candidates:

| Niche | CAGR | Premium price tolerance | Objection richness | All 5 archetypes fit |
|-------|------|------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| **Cognitive / nootropic** | **12-14%** | **$65-79+/mo** | **Highest** | **YES** |
| Women's hormonal | 5.6% | Medium | Medium | No — spec-hero weak |
| Longevity / NAD+ | 18% | Very high but ICP narrow | Medium | No — lifestyle/founder-video thin |
| Sleep / circadian | 5.1% | Low | Low | No — clinical archetype weak |

Cognitive wins because: (1) objection density is highest — "does it work / which ingredients / how long / safe to stack" — meaning spec-hero and clinical archetypes carry maximum weight; (2) premium clinical DTC tier is thin (fewer than 10 real players; Thesis, Mind Lab Pro, HVMN); (3) ICP breadth (knowledge workers, athletes, executives) makes all five archetypes land credibly.

---

### 1. Brand Name

**Selected: Vela**

Latin origin — sail / candle. Both meanings carry directed energy and illumination. One syllable on cadence, phonetically clean, avoids the "neuro/brain/smart" cliche that marks 90% of the category. .com feasible. The candle duality supports "precision-directed mental energy" for spec-hero/clinical variants and "light the way" for lifestyle/founder-video variants.

Candidates considered: Kairos (3 syllables, .com taken), Noor (geographic association risk in US market).

---

### 2. Tagline

**"Clarity. Every hour."**

Outcome + frequency. Mid-tagline period signals confidence, not question. "Every hour" implies all-day sustained effect — the primary differentiator vs single-dose competitors.

---

### 3. Hero Claim

"Vela is a precision-dosed nootropic engineered for sustained focus, working memory, and mental endurance — in the hours that count."

"Precision-dosed" is the spec-hero load-bearing phrase — signals intentional, transparent dosing vs proprietary-blend hiding.

---

### 4. Product

**Vela Focus Formula — 60 Capsules (30-day supply, 2 caps/day)**

Format: Capsules. MD-endorsable. Enables precise per-ingredient dosing disclosure.

| Ingredient | Dose | Role |
|------------|------|------|
| Citicoline (Cognizin branded) | 500 mg | Attention, working memory — 15+ human clinical studies |
| L-Theanine | 200 mg | Focus without jitter, alpha brainwave support |
| Bacopa Monnieri (45% bacosides) | 300 mg | Long-term memory encoding — 12-week RCTs |
| Lion's Mane Mushroom (30% beta-glucan) | 500 mg | NGF support, neuroprotection |
| Rhodiola Rosea (3% rosavins, 1% salidroside) | 200 mg | Mental fatigue resistance, cortisol modulation |

No proprietary blends. All doses at or above clinically studied thresholds. MD-endorsable without reservation.

---

### 5. Pricing

- One-time: **$79 / 30-day supply** ($2.63/day)
- Subscribe & save 15%: **$67/month** ($2.23/day)

Per-serving copy: "Less than your morning coffee. More than it delivers."

Positioned between Mind Lab Pro ($65-69) and Thesis ($79-119). Meaningfully above GNC/Amazon tier ($25-40).

---

### 6. Palette Direction (for token agent)

Reference brands: Ritual (cream + sage warmth), Hims supplement pages (midnight authority), Thesis (warm sand + forest green).

In words:
- Base: warm cream (#F7F4EF range) — not pure white, never sterile
- Primary: deep forest / midnight sage (#1C3A2F range) — authority, not cold pharma blue
- Accent: amber-warm gold (#C8963E range) — the "candle/vela" reference, CTAs and highlights only
- Text: near-black warm (#1A1A18)
- Avoid: electric blue, neon green, energy drink palette, pharmaceutical teal

Flex rule: spec-hero + clinical variants push dark forest base. Lifestyle + founder-video push cream base. Split-hero is the middle register.

---

### 7. Brand Voice (for quill)

Three adjectives: **Precise. Assured. Literate.**

Anti-pattern — never use: "Unlock your potential" and all its variants (unleash, maximize, supercharge, boost). If the sentence could appear on a GNC end-cap, rewrite it.

---

### 8. Top 3 Buyer Objections

**1. Efficacy: "Do nootropics actually work or is this pseudoscience?"**
Root: Category polluted by underdosed proprietary blends. Buyers burned by "clinically studied" language used with sub-threshold doses.
Response architecture: Named ingredients + specific doses + PubMed links + Cognizin branded ingredient (pre-validated by its own clinical program). Spec-hero and clinical variants address this above fold structurally.

**2. Safety: "Is it safe daily? Will it interact with medications?"**
Root: Cognitive supplements are associated with prescription stimulants in buyer perception.
Response architecture: All 5 ingredients non-stimulant, non-habit-forming, GRAS status. MD-endorsement card. NSF Certified for Sport / Informed Sport cert above fold.

**3. Timeframe: "How long before I feel something?"**
Root: Bacopa and Lion's Mane require 8-12 weeks; buyers who expect instant results churn early.
Response architecture: Two-track claims. "Day 1: sharper focus within 45-60 minutes (Citicoline + L-Theanine)." "Week 8: measurable working memory improvement (Bacopa 300mg, 12-week RCT)." Converts the long-term mechanism from objection into subscription reason.

---

### Archetype Fit

| Archetype | Fit | Load-bearing element |
|-----------|-----|---------------------|
| Spec-hero | Strong | Named dosing table, Cognizin, PubMed chips |
| Lifestyle | Strong | Performance identity, amber/sage palette |
| Split-hero | Strong | Capsule (tactile) + precision copy |
| Founder-video | Strong | "I refused to take proprietary blends" narrative |
| Clinical | Strong | MD card, per-ingredient study chip, "4 RCTs" stat |

description: Patterns that caused problems across Boldteq projects — never repeat these
type: feedback
---

## Cross-Stack Antipatterns

### Security
- **Never** trust client-sent user IDs or shop IDs — always get from authenticated session
- **Never** expose service role keys or secret keys to client-side code
- **Never** skip input validation on API endpoints — always use Zod

### Database
- **Never** run `findMany` without a `where` clause on tables with >1000 rows — causes timeouts
- **Never** use `any` type in TypeScript — masks real type errors that become runtime bugs
- **Never** do database schema changes directly in dashboards for production — always use migrations

### Performance
- **Never** do heavy computation in Remix loaders — they run on every navigation

---
name: shadcn v4 Base UI Compatibility
description: Critical API differences between shadcn v4 (Base UI) and shadcn v3 (Radix). Verified 2026-04-27 on Vite + React 19 + Tailwind 4.
type: feedback
---

# shadcn v4 — Base UI API Differences

shadcn v4 (canary/latest as of 2026-04-27) ships primitives from `@base-ui/react`, NOT `@radix-ui`. API differs significantly.

## Accordion (`@base-ui/react/accordion`)
- **NO `type` prop.** Drop `type="single"` — single-open is default.
- **NO `collapsible` prop.** Items are collapsible by default.
- **Multi-open:** use `openMultiple` boolean (default `false`).
- **State attribute:** `data-open` / `data-closed` (not `data-state=open`).
- `onValueChange` still works, fires `AccordionValue<T>` not `string | undefined`.

## Button (`@base-ui/react/button`)
- **NO `asChild` prop.** Use `buttonVariants()` className on a native `<Link>` or `<a>`.
  ```tsx
  import { buttonVariants } from "@/components/ui/button";
  <Link to="/foo" className={cn(buttonVariants({ size: "lg" }), "custom-class")}>...</Link>
  ```

## TabsTrigger (`@base-ui/react/tabs`)
- **Active state:** use `data-active:` selector, NOT `data-[state=active]:`.
  ```tsx
  className="data-active:bg-forest-800 data-active:text-cream-50"
  ```
  Note: may need `!` override if shadcn default active styles conflict.

## Dialog / Sheet
- Both built on `@base-ui/react/dialog`. API similar to Radix (open, onOpenChange).
- Close button uses `render` prop: `<DialogPrimitive.Close render={<Button ... />}>`.
- Backdrop is `DialogPrimitive.Backdrop` (not `DialogOverlay`/`SheetOverlay` from Radix).

## Tailwind 4 `@theme inline {}` bridge block
- **NEVER remove.** shadcn components reference variables like `--ring`, `--border`, `--primary` etc.
  via this bridge block which maps `var(--color-*)` utility classes to CSS custom properties.
- Remove it → all shadcn button/input/card variants break silently.
- Keep structure: `@theme {}` (Vela tokens) → `@theme inline {}` (bridge, untouched) → `:root {}` → `.dark {}`.

## tsconfig requirements
- `"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true` — requires `?? fallback` on any `array[i]` or `Record[key]` access.
- `"strict": true` — covers no-implicit-any, strict-null-checks etc.
- Alias: `"paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] }` needed for shadcn CLI detection.
- May need `"ignoreDeprecations": "6.0"` in `tsconfig.app.json` for TypeScript 6 `baseUrl` warning.

---
name: 5-Variant CRO Landing Structure
description: Reusable scaffold for testing 5 distinct buyer psychologies on one DTC brand. Verified on Vela (nootropic) build 2026-04-27.
type: feedback
---

# 5-Variant CRO Landing Structure

Portable pattern for DTC ecom: same brand, same below-fold, 5 distinct above-fold conversion psychologies.

## Why: CRO mandate
A/B/C/D/E test 5 distinct opening moves before committing to one hero treatment.
Sharing below-fold means the variable is ONLY the hero — clean signal.

## Hero archetype map (5 slots)

| Slot | Archetype | Buyer | Above-fold key |
|------|-----------|-------|----------------|
| V1 | Spec-hero | Rational/data | Numbers, facts table, 0 blends claim |
| V2 | Lifestyle | Emotional/aspirational | Full-bleed product, single-line promise |
| V3 | Split-hero | Skeptical/transparency | Ingredient photo left, dose ladder right |
| V4 | Founder-video | Narrative/story | Looping b-roll, founder quote, origin |
| V5 | Clinical/authority | Credentialed | MD endorsement, cert badges, RCT stats |

## Shared below-fold rhythm (all 5)
BenefitsGrid → TrustBar → IngredientModule → ReviewsSection → FAQAccordion → CTABlock → Footer

## Cart state isolation
- Each variant = a standalone React tree with its own `<CartProvider>`
- No cross-variant state — each is self-contained for measurement purity

## CRO mechanics (shared across all variants)
SubscribeToggle (subscribe default) · BundleSelector (1/2/3-pack) · StickyAddToCart (mobile, IntersectionObserver) · CartDrawer (Sheet, free-ship bar, upsell) · ExitIntent (Dialog, desktop, once/session, suppressed if cart open) · FAQAccordion (soft CTA after 3 opens) · IngredientModule (accordion expand-in-place)

## Index gallery route
`/` shows all 5 variant cards with: archetype label, psychology, hook line, hero theme preview.
Enables stakeholder review at single URL. Each card deep-links to full variant.

## Supplement-specific confirmed patterns
- Safety cert (NSF/Informed Sport) in hero zone — 5/6 top brands do this
- Realistic review distribution 62/24/9/3/2 (not clean 90/8/2)
- Subscribe-default with "cancel anytime" framing outperforms one-time default
- Per-unit cost in daily format: "$2.23/day" > "$67/month"
- Two-timeline claim: "Day 1: focus. Week 8: memory." resolves timeframe objection AND extends subscription reasoning

## File structure template
```
src/
  variants/         ← V1-V5, each a full page with CartProvider
  components/shared/ ← all CRO mechanics (Cart, Toggle, Bundle, FAQ etc.)
  pages/Index.tsx   ← variant gallery
  data/mock.ts      ← Product type + pricing math functions
  data/hero-copy.ts ← 5 typed above-fold copy bundles
  data/page-copy.ts ← shared below-fold copy (benefits, ingredients, reviews, FAQ)
  lib/use-cart-state.ts ← CartState hook
  lib/types.ts      ← shared types (Product, CartState, BundleSize, etc.)
  index.css         ← @theme tokens (Tailwind 4 CSS-first)
```

## Reuse this for
Any DTC vertical: wellness, beauty, apparel, food, fitness equipment.
Swap: brand bible, palette tokens, hero copy bundles, product data.
Keep: component architecture, CRO mechanics, below-fold rhythm.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
